developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0059"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.

doctl account get
aws configure list

checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0069"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0072"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]

      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0075"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0079"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0082"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0085"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_iam.do_iam_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean IAM & Tokens: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Identity, Teams & Scoped API Tokens)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_vpc.do_vpc_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean VPC: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 VPC & Private Network Isolation)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_vpc.do_vpc_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean VPC: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 VPC & Private Network Isolation)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_vpc.do_vpc_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean VPC: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 VPC & Private Network Isolation)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
