opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0179"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0181"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

    end

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0186"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0188"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0190"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0193"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics

Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

doctl account get
aws configure list

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0195"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0197"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0200"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

aws configure list

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0202"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))

deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0207"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Managed Databases"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0209"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.

tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.

package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_database.do_database_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Managed Databases: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Managed Databases (Postgres & MySQL))
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-database", label: "DigitalOcean Managed Databases", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application database connection
developer_guide.contract: Driver, hostname, engine-specific port, TLS mode and transaction semantics
dependencies: A provisioned database, schema and application role
Private routing or an explicitly configured access path
A bounded application connection pool
steps: Provision the database and apply versioned schema migrations.
Inject runtime credentials or configure supported identity authentication.
Configure certificate verification and a bounded connection pool.
tests: Run a transaction and verify rollback on failure.
Reject a read-only role attempting a write.
Test connection exhaustion and instance replacement.
failures: Connection refusal: verify database listener, route and security rules.
Pool exhaustion: inspect leaked connections, query latency and concurrency.
