developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      requirement --> check

      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-loadbalancer", label: "DigitalOcean Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource

      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Load Balancer"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0326"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-loadbalancer", label: "DigitalOcean Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Load Balancer"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0329"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Load Balancer"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0330"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-loadbalancer", label: "DigitalOcean Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Load Balancer"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0334"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-loadbalancer", label: "DigitalOcean Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

doctl account get
aws configure list

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Load Balancer"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0338"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-loadbalancer", label: "DigitalOcean Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Load Balancer"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0342"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-loadbalancer", label: "DigitalOcean Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Load Balancer"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0343"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-loadbalancer", label: "DigitalOcean Load Balancer", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_loadbalancer.do_loadbalancer_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Load Balancer: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Cloud Load Balancers & SSL Offload)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_dns.do_dns_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud DNS: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Cloud DNS & Domain Management)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_dns.do_dns_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud DNS: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Cloud DNS & Domain Management)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_dns.do_dns_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud DNS: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Cloud DNS & Domain Management)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Cloud DNS"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Cloud DNS: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0347"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-dns", label: "DigitalOcean Cloud DNS", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_dns.do_dns_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud DNS: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Cloud DNS & Domain Management)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement

    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0348"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-dns", label: "DigitalOcean Cloud DNS", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_dns.do_dns_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud DNS: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Cloud DNS & Domain Management)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: DNS discovery and application connection
developer_guide.contract: Zone, record name, record type, answer, TTL and resolver scope
dependencies: An authoritative zone and record set
A resolver and network links for private zones
A separately reachable application endpoint
steps: Create the zone and records with deliberate TTLs.
Configure resolver scope and any private network links.
Test name resolution separately from the application connection.
tests: Query from the actual client environment and inspect the answer and TTL.
Verify a private name is only resolvable from the intended scope.
failures: NXDOMAIN: inspect zone delegation, private links and record name.
Correct answer but failed request: inspect application routing and listener.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_dns.do_dns_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud DNS: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Cloud DNS & Domain Management)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Cloud DNS"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Cloud DNS: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0350"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-dns", label: "DigitalOcean Cloud DNS", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
