opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0411"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-backup", label: "DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0415"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-backup", label: "DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.

package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0422"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-backup", label: "DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0426"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-backup", label: "DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_backup.do_backup_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Droplet Snapshots & Automated Backups)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0430"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-backup", label: "DigitalOcean Snapshots & Backups", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Backup and restore integration
developer_guide.contract: Supported resource, backup schedule, retention and measured RPO/RTO
dependencies: A supported source resource and backup service role
A backup destination with explicit retention settings
steps: Configure supported backup jobs and a destination.
Monitor job completion and recovery point availability.
Restore to an isolated test target and validate application data.
tests: Restore a known dataset and compare application-level checksums.
Measure recovery time and verify failed job notifications.
failures: Backup failure: inspect service role, source support and key permissions.
Restore failure: inspect destination prerequisites and key availability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Monitoring"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Monitoring: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0431"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-monitoring", label: "DigitalOcean Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Monitoring"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Monitoring: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0434"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-monitoring", label: "DigitalOcean Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0436"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-monitoring", label: "DigitalOcean Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Monitoring"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Monitoring: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0438"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-monitoring", label: "DigitalOcean Monitoring", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application telemetry and analysis
developer_guide.contract: Trace or request ID, event schema, timestamp, metric labels and retention
dependencies: Application instrumentation or an explicit ingestion connector
A telemetry destination and scoped writer identity
steps: Emit structured events with a stable correlation ID.
Configure ingestion, retention and query permissions.
Create an actionable query or alert and test it with a known event.
tests: Trace one request through application logs and dependency calls.
Confirm an injected failure triggers the intended alert.
failures: Missing telemetry: inspect exporter configuration and ingestion permissions.
High ingestion cost: inspect duplicate exporters and high-cardinality labels.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_monitoring.do_monitoring_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Monitoring: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Monitoring, Alerts & Metrics Agent)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
