developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_waf.do_waf_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud WAF: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Cloud WAF & Edge Filtering)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Cloud WAF"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Cloud WAF: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0898"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-waf", label: "DigitalOcean Cloud WAF", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_waf.do_waf_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud WAF: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Cloud WAF & Edge Filtering)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_waf.do_waf_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud WAF: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Cloud WAF & Edge Filtering)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_waf.do_waf_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud WAF: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Cloud WAF & Edge Filtering)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_waf.do_waf_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud WAF: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Cloud WAF & Edge Filtering)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Edge request routing and origin access
developer_guide.contract: Public hostname, certificate, cache key, origin host and auth policy
dependencies: A reachable application or object origin
A public certificate and explicit DNS records
Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_waf.do_waf_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Cloud WAF: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Cloud WAF & Edge Filtering)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Cloud WAF"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Cloud WAF: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0903"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-waf", label: "DigitalOcean Cloud WAF", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Configured origin access and any attached WAF or identity policy
steps: Deploy and test the origin independently.
Configure edge routing, origin authentication and cache behavior.
Attach the intended protection and verify allowed and blocked requests.
tests: Test cache hits, cache misses and authenticated routes.
Verify disallowed requests are rejected and the origin access policy holds.
failures: 403: distinguish edge policy rejection from origin permission failure.
Stale content: inspect cache keys, TTL and invalidation behavior.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

doctl account get
aws configure list

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Audit Logs"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0908"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean Audit Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.

failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Audit Logs"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0912"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean Audit Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Audit Logs"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0917"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean Audit Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Audit Logs"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0921"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean Audit Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

doctl account get
aws configure list

checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Audit Logs"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0926"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean Audit Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Audit Logs"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0930"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean Audit Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.

Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.

Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

doctl account get
aws configure list

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Audit Logs"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0935"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean Audit Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: API event collection
developer_guide.contract: Event type, resource identity, event time, destination and retention
dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

doctl account get
aws configure list

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: Supported event sources with required categories enabled
A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
Configure destination permissions and retention.
Generate a known API event and correlate it with a recorded request.
tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

doctl account get

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

A destination and delivery permissions

tests: Verify the known event arrives within the expected delivery window.
Test destination permission failure and delivery monitoring.
failures: Missing event: inspect category selection, exclusions and delivery permissions.
Unexpected delay: compare event time, ingestion time and service delivery behavior.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Audit Logs"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0939"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean Audit Logs", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_audit.do_audit_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Audit Logs: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Audit Logs & API Event Tracking)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

A destination and delivery permissions
steps: Enable the required management or data event categories.
