developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Gradient AI"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0976"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-ai", label: "DigitalOcean Gradient AI", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

doctl account get
aws configure list

checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Gradient AI"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0979"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-ai", label: "DigitalOcean Gradient AI", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

doctl account get
aws configure list

checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Gradient AI"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0981"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-ai", label: "DigitalOcean Gradient AI", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Gradient AI"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0984"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-ai", label: "DigitalOcean Gradient AI", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

doctl account get
aws configure list

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Gradient AI"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0987"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-ai", label: "DigitalOcean Gradient AI", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_ai.do_ai_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Gradient AI: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Gradient AI & GPU Droplets)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_ingress_boundary_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering (Tier-1 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_firewall"
  not r.change.after.inbound_rule
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure inbound_rule for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Security Posture"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce Restrictive Ingress Filtering"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0990"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-compliance", label: "DigitalOcean Security Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_vpc_isolation_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce Private Network (VPC) Binding (Tier-2 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.vpc_uuid
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure vpc_uuid for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_tls_enforcement_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Require TLS 1.3 Encryption & Secure Ciphers (Tier-3 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_version
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure tls_version for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_snapshot_lifecycle_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention (Tier-4 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Security Posture"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce Automated Snapshot Retention"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0993"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-compliance", label: "DigitalOcean Security Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_spaces_private_access_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4 (Tier-5 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_spaces_bucket"
  not r.change.after.acl
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure acl for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Security Posture"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Security Posture: Block Public Bucket Access & Require S3 SigV4"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0994"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-compliance", label: "DigitalOcean Security Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_iam_least_privilege_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce Scoped OAuth & Minimal Token Delegation (Tier-6 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.scopes
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure scopes for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      check -->|Yes| review

      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-compliance", label: "DigitalOcean Security Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enable Storage Volume LUKS / AES-256 Encryption (Tier-7 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_volume"
  not r.change.after.filesystem_type
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure filesystem_type for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0996"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-compliance", label: "DigitalOcean Security Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_audit_logging_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Mandate Audit Log Forwarding to Telemetry Sink (Tier-8 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_project"
  not r.change.after.audit_forwarding
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure audit_forwarding for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_doks_admission_gate_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS (Tier-9 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.auto_upgrade
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure auto_upgrade for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["DigitalOcean: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for DigitalOcean Security Posture"]
      requirement["DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce Strict Kubernetes Pod Admission via DOKS"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:do-iam", label: "DigitalOcean API token or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0998"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-compliance", label: "DigitalOcean Security Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_db_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Require Multi-Zone Standby for High Availability (Tier-10 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_database_cluster"
  not r.change.after.region
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure region for compliance standard CIS DigitalOcean Benchmark v1.2", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-0999"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-compliance", label: "DigitalOcean Security Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_ssh_key_only_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce SSH Key-Only Authentication without Passwords (Tier-11 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_droplet"
  not r.change.after.ssh_keys
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure ssh_keys for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: DO-BP-1000"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["DigitalOcean: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:do-compliance", label: "DigitalOcean Security Posture", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      evidence@{ icon: "logos:do-audit", label: "DigitalOcean audit logs and droplet activity", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package digitalocean.do_compliance.do_compliance_dns_dnssec_protection_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: DigitalOcean Security Posture: Enforce DNSSEC & Cloud DNS Zone Hardening (Tier-12 Security Posture & CIS Benchmarks)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "digitalocean_domain"
  not r.change.after.dnssec
  msg := sprintf("Resource %v must configure dnssec for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via DigitalOcean CLI (doctl) or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
doctl account get
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
